text:
jin: Heads-up: during today's mini-canary we got a near-tie between model v2a (int4) and v2b (nf4-lite). Overall metrics within noise; longdoc MRR tilts toward v2a but v2b latency ~12% lower. Need a deterministic tiebreaker for promote. Thoughts?

sasha: +1 on deterministic. Proposal: if quality delta < 0.25% prefer lower-latency; else prefer quality. Add slice overrides: if longdoc delta > 0.4% pick quality regardless.

ravi: Agree. Also recommend including cost delta and kv-warm penalty in decision. We saw v2a had coldstart kv misses in the smoke run. small log: `kv_warm_misses: v2a=132, v2b=8`

jin: Draft config sketch below — we can plumb into rollout-service:

```yaml
promote_policy:
  tiebreaker:
    primary_metric: "mrr"
    delta_threshold: 0.0025        # 0.25% absolute
    prefer: "latency"            # prefer lower-latency when within threshold
    slice_overrides:
      - slice: "longdoc"
        threshold: 0.004          # 0.4% -> prefer quality for longdoc
  cost_sensitivity:
    max_cost_increase_pct: 5
  coldstart_penalty:
    kv_warm_miss_weight: 0.1
```

ashley: :thumbsup: keep it simple. Also add an abort rule: hallucination_rate > 0.3% -> immediate abort/rollback.

luke: +1. And add deterministic fallback ordering as last resort (lexicographic model id) so different runs don't flip-flop. Also log `tiebreaker_reason` in the rollout audit events.

deploy-bot: Canary report uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/1742100000-sibling-check.html (summary: mrr_diff=0.18%, latency_p99_diff=-12%, cost_diff=+1.8%)

sasha: I'll implement the policy in rollout-service and add unit tests for slice overrides and cost bounds. pinging @ravi for the eval slices to include in gating.

ravi: On it. I'll add longdoc, code-example, and convo slices and replay ~10k samples overnight. Will post slice-level deltas once done.

jin: Sweet. Quick operational guard: auto-fallback triggers if either (a) weighted MRR drops >=0.5% across top-5 slices OR (b) p99 latency increases >=100ms. I'll put those in the PR for the promote job.

sasha: Nice. After we ship, let's run a quiet-burn at 1% traffic for 2h before full promote. Keeps us safe from sample bias.

jin: Agreed. Thanks all — I'll open PR w/ config and smoke test checklist.
